missions.name: Artemis Lunar Surface Habitat
missions.summary: Exploration atmosphere at 10.2 psi and 34% O2 (>40% increase over sea-level O2 mole fraction) to minimize EVA pre-breathe overhead. Partial gravity (0.16g) induces buoyant inflow that prevents radiative self-extinguishment observed in 0g still air.

missions.name: Lunar Pressurized Rover Cabin
missions.summary: Compact cabin volume operated at 8.2 to 10.2 psi and 34% O2 for direct suitport transfers. High airlock dust ingress requires photoelectric discrimination between cabin smoke and sub-10 micron lunar regolith.

missions.name: ISS / Commercial LEO Station
missions.summary: Earth-normal 14.7 psi and 21% O2 in microgravity. Absence of buoyant flow makes flame survival strictly dependent on HVAC ventilation velocity (5 to 25 cm/s) and diffusive transport.

missions.name: Mars Surface Habitat
missions.summary: Operates at 0.38g where convective buoyant plumes approach 60% of terrestrial velocity. Combined with 30% O2, upward flame spread accelerates sharply relative to microgravity.

missions.name: xEMU / Exploration Spacesuit
missions.summary: Pure 100% O2 at 4.3 psi to preserve suit mobility. Extreme oxygen mole fraction lowers material ignition thresholds dramatically under high-velocity helmet purge flow.

investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
sample_geometries: Flat sheet (22x50 mm)
Cast PMMA rod (6.4 mm dia)
PMMA sphere (12.7 mm dia)
investigations.objectives: Characterize Concurrent and opposed-flow flame spread and extinction over solid fuels in microgravity under controlled low-speed ventilation.
investigations.key_findings: Demonstrated that solid materials self-extinguish in still 0g air due to radiative heat loss, but sustain steady blue flames at ventilation flows as low as 1 to 3 cm/s, yielding a lower Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) in 0g than in 1g.

investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
fuels: Clear and black cast PMMA sheets
sample_geometries: Flat strips (10 to 30 mm width)
Thin films (0.1 to 2.0 mm)
Cylindrical rods
investigations.objectives: Determine flammability maps (O2 vs flow speed) and flame spread scaling for spacecraft-relevant fabrics and polymers in microgravity.
investigations.key_findings: Established U-shaped flammability boundaries where low-speed microgravity flow (2 to 8 cm/s) sustains combustion at O2 concentrations 2.5% below normal 1g upward testing limits (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1).

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration I
sample_geometries: Large-scale continuous panel (400 mm wide x 940 mm long)
intra_variables: Elapsed burn time in finite cabin volume
investigations.objectives: Validate whether small-sample ISS glovebox flammability tests (BASS-II) accurately scale to meter-class fires inside an uncrewed cargo spacecraft.
investigations.key_findings: Flame reached a steady spread rate rather than accelerating indefinitely, confirming that radiative heat loss and finite boundary-layer oxygen diffusion limit meter-scale flame growth in 0g.

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration II
fuels: PMMA sheets (flat and grooved, 1 to 10 mm)
sample_geometries: 9 panel strips (50 mm wide x 290 mm long)
investigations.objectives: Evaluate the Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) limits and thickness effects across 9 standard spacecraft cabin materials in realistic vehicle ventilation.
investigations.key_findings: Grooved PMMA and thin silicone sustained propagation while thick flat PMMA quenched, proving surface geometry strongly modifies 0g ignition margins.

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration III
sample_geometries: Large-scale panel (400 mm x 940 mm)
intra_variables: Higher ventilation velocity (30 cm/s vs 20 cm/s in Saffire-I)
intra_constants: Sample material and dimensions (0.4 x 0.94 m)
investigations.objectives: Quantify how a 50% increase in spacecraft ventilation speed (30 cm/s vs 20 cm/s) alters large-scale flame spread rate and cabin heat release.
investigations.key_findings: Flame spread velocity scaled nearly linearly with forced oxygen supply rate at 30 cm/s, generating higher peak cabin pressure rise and faster O2 consumption.

investigations.title: ACME: Burning Rate Emulator
sample_geometries: Flat porous brass burners (25 mm and 50 mm diameter)
intra_variables: Fuel mass flux (emulating heat of gasification)
sensors: Heat flux gauge on burner face
investigations.objectives: Simulate condensed-phase solid/liquid material flammability in still microgravity atmospheres by matching gaseous fuel flow to heat feedback.
investigations.key_findings: Demonstrated how material heat of gasification, surface heat loss, and radiation control steady burning vs radiative extinction in quiescent 0g atmospheres up to 40% O2.

investigations.title: ACME: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
sample_geometries: Porous spherical burner (6.4 mm diameter) in inverse inside-out configuration
intra_variables: Internal burner O2 mole fraction (up to 85% O2)
sensors: UV intensified camera (OH* and CH2O* chemiluminescence)
investigations.objectives: Achieve steady non-premixed gaseous cool flames in microgravity and probe high-oxygen combustion limits up to 85% O2.
investigations.key_findings: Contains the highest oxygen concentration tests in PSI (up to 85% O2 flowing from the burner into fuel-nitrogen atmospheres), directly informing high-O2 spacesuit and pre-breathe ignition physics.

investigations.title: ACME: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
sample_geometries: Co-flow cylindrical nozzle with parallel high-voltage mesh electrode
investigations.gravity_regime: 0g + Electrically Simulated Partial Gravity (0.05g to 1.0g equivalent)
investigations.objectives: Drive naturally occurring chemi-ions in microgravity flames using an electric field (ionic wind) to mimic buoyant convection without gravity.
investigations.key_findings: Established direct equivalence between applied electric field strength (V/cm) and gravitational acceleration (0.16g Lunar and 0.38g Martian buoyancy), reducing soot and shifting blowoff/extinction limits.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
sample_geometries: Free-floating and fiber-supported spherical droplets (1.5 to 5.0 mm dia)
intra_variables: Suppressant gas ratio (CO2 vs Helium vs N2)
investigations.objectives: Quantify droplet burning rates and the minimum inert-gas concentration (CO2, He) required to extinguish fires in spacecraft cabins.
investigations.key_findings: Discovered unexpected second-stage low-temperature cool flames (500 to 800 K) after radiative hot-flame extinction of heptane droplets, posing a hidden vapor re-ignition hazard after fire suppression.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
sample_geometries: Isolated spherical droplets (2.0 to 4.5 mm dia) and droplet pairs
intra_variables: Ambient O2 and diluent heat capacity
investigations.objectives: Investigate radiative extinction diameters, droplet-droplet interactions, and multi-stage combustion kinetics in microgravity.
investigations.key_findings: Mapped the critical droplet diameter where radiative heat loss triggers sudden transition from hot diffusion burning to persistent cool-flame oxidation.

investigations.title: Cool Flames Investigation
sample_geometries: Large free-floating spherical droplets (3.0 to 5.5 mm dia)
investigations.objectives: Directly observe and model invisible low-temperature alkane cool flames that govern post-suppression re-ignition in microgravity.
investigations.key_findings: Confirmed that heavy hydrocarbon droplets sustain invisible cool flames for several seconds in 0g and produce dense unburned white aerosol clouds upon final quenching.

investigations.title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
sample_geometries: Wire segments and small coupon strips heated on thermal coils
sensors: ISS photoelectric and Space Shuttle ionization detectors
investigations.objectives: Measure smoke particle size distributions (count median diameter and mass concentration) from overheating spacecraft wiring in 0g.
investigations.key_findings: Absence of buoyant plume rise increases residence time in the hot zone, causing 0g smoke particles to agglomerate into significantly larger diameters (0.3 to 1.2 microns) than in 1g, shifting optimal detector calibration thresholds.

investigations.title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
sample_geometries: Overheated wire coils and avionics coupon samples
investigations.objectives: Refine multi-wavelength scattering algorithms to detect pre-ignition smoldering avionics while rejecting non-fire aerosols.
investigations.key_findings: Multi-angle / multi-wavelength scattering ratios separate sub-micron pyrolysis smoke from larger mechanical dust particles.

investigations.title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT & DAFT-2)
sample_geometries: Suspended polydisperse particulate aerosols (0.1 to 20 microns)
investigations.objectives: Repurpose the SAME smoke-detection instrument suite to characterize airborne dust in microgravity and prevent dust-induced false smoke alarms.
investigations.key_findings: Proved how dual-channel particle size discrimination prevents lunar/Martian surface dust (>1.5 microns) from triggering false cabin smoke alarms like the Artemis II event.

investigations.title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
sample_geometries: Round nozzle tubes (1.6 to 6.0 mm dia) in laminar co-flow
intra_variables: Fuel flow rate at soot breakthrough (smoke point)
intra_constants: 76x76 mm flow duct built for MSG
investigations.objectives: Determine laminar flame smoke points (transition from non-smoking to soot-emitting flames) in microgravity co-flow.
investigations.key_findings: Built the modular fan-driven MSG flow duct subsequently shared by SLICE, BASS, and BASS-II; showed 0g flames emit heavy soot at much shorter flame lengths than in 1g.

investigations.title: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
sample_geometries: Co-flow axisymmetric nozzles (1.6 to 4.5 mm dia)
intra_constants: SPICE flow duct hardware in MSG
investigations.objectives: Measure flame liftoff height, stabilization base structure, and blowoff limits of laminar jet diffusion flames in microgravity.
investigations.key_findings: Revealed how triple-flame propagation speed at the flame base governs whether a lifted flame stabilizes or blows off under spacecraft ventilation speeds.

historical_incidents.cause: Electrical arc near lower equipment bay ignited Velcro and nylon netting in high-pressure pure oxygen.
historical_incidents.engineering_lesson: Drove strict material flammability screening (NASA-STD-6001) and limits on cabin oxygen partial pressure, directly motivating BASS-II, Saffire, and CFI-G high-oxygen testing.

historical_incidents.cause: Damaged Teflon wire insulation ignited during heater thermostatic cycling inside pure oxygen tank.
historical_incidents.engineering_lesson: Highlighted wire-insulation ignition hazards in high-oxygen environments and motivated early pyrolysis aerosol detection in SAME and SAME-R.

historical_incidents.cause: Lithium perchlorate solid-fuel oxygen generator (Vika TGK candle) fault produced a blowtorch flame and dense non-settling smoke.
historical_incidents.engineering_lesson: Demonstrated that 0g smoke does not stratify and that water/foam extinguishers fail to reach enclosed rack fires, inspiring FLEX gas suppression and ISS fine-water-mist extinguishers.

historical_incidents.atmosphere: Deep-space crew cabin (~80,000 miles from Earth)
historical_incidents.cause: Transient cabin aerosol / particulate triggered spacecraft smoke alarm in deep space.
historical_incidents.engineering_lesson: Underscores the urgent operational need for DAFT-2 and SAME-R multi-wavelength particle discrimination so crews can instantly distinguish false dust alarms from real electrical pyrolysis.

earth_spinoffs.title: Lightweight Composite Firefighter Air Tanks (SCBA)
earth_spinoffs.nasa_origin: Apollo Portable Life Support System (PLSS) filament-wound aluminum-composite oxygen vessels
earth_spinoffs.terrestrial_impact: Reduced firefighter breathing apparatus weight by 40%, increasing mobility and endurance inside burning buildings.

earth_spinoffs.title: Dust-Discriminating Industrial & Mining Smoke Detectors
earth_spinoffs.nasa_origin: Skylab / Space Shuttle / ISS SAME & DAFT aerosol particle-size discrimination sensors
earth_spinoffs.terrestrial_impact: Eliminates nuisance alarms in dusty underground mines, manufacturing plants, and cargo holds by separating >2 micron dust from sub-micron pyrolysis aerosols.

earth_spinoffs.title: PBI & Advanced Thermal Firefighter Protective Attire
earth_spinoffs.nasa_origin: Post-Apollo 1 non-flammable polybenzimidazole (PBI) and Nomex spacesuit fabric engineering
earth_spinoffs.terrestrial_impact: Standardized high-LOI thermal barrier fabrics that resist charring and shrinkage in structural firefighting suits worldwide.

earth_spinoffs.title: Portable Fine-Water-Mist Fire Extinguishers
earth_spinoffs.nasa_origin: ISS Portable Fire Extinguisher (PFE) droplet-size optimization derived from MDCA / FLEX research
earth_spinoffs.terrestrial_impact: Produces 20 to 50 micron water mist droplets that evaporate rapidly to absorb heat and displace oxygen without damaging sensitive data centers, hospitals, or avionics bays.
